findings.reason: the third case is the one this revision added, and a node reading "two fixture projects" can drop the missing-directory launch, leaving the new rule's gate unable to fire.
findings.text: §5's done-when says doctor "gives doctor a fixture user config and two fixture projects" and then lists three distinct project launches (uv run imas-codex serve; uv run --no-sync --project ${HOME}/Code/imas-codex imas-codex serve; uv run --no-sync --project ${HOME}/Code/absent serve) and later refers to "the third" project, so the fixture it describes cannot be built as written

findings.reason: without naming the expansion the check sees the literal string ${HOME}/Code/imas-codex, which never exists, so it flags the pass-case too and the whole done-when collapses.
findings.text: §5 says the corrected command's checkout is written "through a variable Claude Code expands in MCP configuration, such as ${HOME}", but the missing-directory rule ("flags ... a launch whose --project or --directory names a path that does not exist") is never told to expand that variable, yet the fixture only works if it does: the second project passes because ${HOME}/Code/imas-codex exists under the temporary home while the third fails on ${HOME}/Code/absent

findings.reason: read literally the check finds no .mcp.json for the two projects §6 and §1 exist to catch, so its gate would pass on an empty set.

findings.reason: no existing reader counts storage-slow results, so the census still needs its own counter and only the justifying clause is overstated; naming velocity's walker would improve reuse but the mechanism stands.
findings.text: §2 justifies reading tool-result blocks itself because "no existing reader parses tool results", but reckon/velocity.py:1586 already walks every in-window, non-sidechain transcript record's content blocks and extracts tool_result text (the promotion-receipt walker at velocity.py:1555–1605)
